1 Conjugate Bayesian Multivariate Linear Regression

A conjugate Bayesian multivariate linear model (the MNIW model) is given by:

\[Y \mid \beta, \Sigma, X \sim MN_{n,q}(X\beta, I_n, \Sigma)\] \[\beta \mid \Sigma \sim MN_{p,q}(M_0 m_0, M_0, \Sigma)\] \[\Sigma \sim IW(\nu_0, \Psi_0)\]

Unknown parameters include the regression coefficient matrix and the covariance matrix, i.e., \(\theta = \{\beta, \Sigma\}\).

The likelihood of the data is:

\[p(Y \mid \beta, \Sigma) \propto |\Sigma|^{-n/2} \exp\left\{ -\frac{1}{2} \text{tr}\left[ \Sigma^{-1} (Y - X\beta)^{\top} (Y - X\beta) \right] \right\}\]

The joint posterior density is \(p(\beta, \Sigma \mid Y) \propto p(\Sigma) \times p(\beta \mid \Sigma) \times p(Y \mid \beta, \Sigma)\).

2 Deriving the Joint Posterior \(p(\beta, \Sigma \mid Y)\)

\[\begin{aligned} p(\beta, \Sigma \mid Y) &\propto IW(\Sigma \mid \nu_0, \Psi_0) \times MN(\beta \mid M_0 m_0, M_0, \Sigma) \times MN(Y \mid X\beta, I_n, \Sigma) \\ &\propto |\Sigma|^{-\frac{\nu_0 + q + 1}{2}} \exp\left\{ -\frac{1}{2} \text{tr}\left( \Sigma^{-1} \Psi_0 \right) \right\} \\ &\quad \times |\Sigma|^{-\frac{p}{2}} \exp\left\{ -\frac{1}{2} \text{tr}\left[ \Sigma^{-1} (\beta - M_0 m_0)^{\top} M_0^{-1} (\beta - M_0 m_0) \right] \right\} \\ &\quad \times |\Sigma|^{-\frac{n}{2}} \exp\left\{ -\frac{1}{2} \text{tr}\left[ \Sigma^{-1} (Y - X\beta)^{\top} (Y - X\beta) \right] \right\} \\ &\propto |\Sigma|^{-\frac{\nu_0 + n + p + q + 1}{2}} \exp\left\{ -\frac{1}{2} \text{tr}\left( \Sigma^{-1} \left[ \Psi_0 + Q(\beta, Y) \right] \right) \right\} \end{aligned}\]

where the quadratic terms in \(\beta\) are combined as:

\[Q(\beta, Y) = (\beta - M_0 m_0)^{\top} M_0^{-1} (\beta - M_0 m_0) + (Y - X\beta)^{\top} (Y - X\beta)\]

3 Matrix Completion of Square

Expanding and recombining \(Q(\beta, Y)\) (noting that \(M_0\) is symmetric, so \((M_0 m_0)^\top M_0^{-1} \beta = m_0^\top M_0 M_0^{-1} \beta = m_0^\top \beta\)):

\[\begin{aligned} Q(\beta, Y) &= (\beta - M_0 m_0)^{\top} M_0^{-1} (\beta - M_0 m_0) + (Y - X\beta)^{\top} (Y - X\beta) \\ &= \beta^{\top} M_0^{-1} \beta - \beta^{\top} m_0 - m_0^{\top} \beta + m_0^{\top} M_0 m_0 + Y^{\top} Y - Y^{\top} X \beta - \beta^{\top} X^{\top} Y + \beta^{\top} X^{\top} X \beta \\ &= \beta^{\top} (M_0^{-1} + X^{\top} X) \beta - \beta^{\top} (m_0 + X^{\top} Y) - (m_0^{\top} + Y^{\top} X) \beta + (m_0^{\top} M_0 m_0 + Y^{\top} Y) \\ &= (\beta - Mm)^{\top} M^{-1} (\beta - Mm) + S^\ast \end{aligned}\]

where the updated parameters \(M\), \(m\), and \(S^\ast\) are defined as:

\[M^{-1} = M_0^{-1} + X^{\top} X, \quad m = m_0 + X^{\top} Y, \quad S^\ast = m_0^{\top} M_0 m_0 + Y^{\top} Y - m^{\top} M m\]

4 Factorizing the Joint Posterior

Substituting the completed square back into the joint posterior yields:

\[p(\beta, \Sigma \mid Y) \propto \left( |\Sigma|^{-\frac{\nu + q + 1}{2}} \exp\left\{ -\frac{1}{2} \text{tr}\left[ \Sigma^{-1} \Psi \right] \right\} \right) \times \left( |\Sigma|^{-\frac{p}{2}} \exp\left\{ -\frac{1}{2} \text{tr}\left[ \Sigma^{-1} (\beta - Mm)^{\top} M^{-1} (\beta - Mm) \right] \right\} \right)\]

where:

\[\nu = \nu_0 + n, \quad \Psi = \Psi_0 + S^\ast = \Psi_0 + m_0^{\top} M_0 m_0 + Y^{\top} Y - m^{\top} M m\]

This factorizes into \(IW(\Sigma \mid \nu, \Psi) \times MN(\beta \mid Mm, M, \Sigma)\).

5 Federated Learning: Decentralized Divide & Conquer

In a Federated Learning architecture, a central server orchestrates statistical estimation across \(T\) local client servers. Raw client datasets \((Y_t, X_t)\) remain strictly on client \(t\) to ensure data privacy.

The central server holds global prior parameters: \(M_0^{-1}\), \(m_0\), \(\nu_0\), and \(\Psi_0\).

5.1 Local Client Computations

Each client \(t\) independently computes localized sufficient statistics:

\[\Delta M_t^{-1} = X_t^{\top} X_t, \quad \Delta m_t = X_t^{\top} Y_t, \quad \Delta Q_t = Y_t^{\top} Y_t, \quad n_t = \text{nrow}(X_t)\]

Client \(t\) transmits only the low-dimensional tuple \((\Delta M_t^{-1}, \Delta m_t, \Delta Q_t, n_t)\) back to the central server. For \(p=10\) predictors and \(q=5\) outcomes, the client transmits a \(10 \times 10\) matrix, a \(10 \times 5\) matrix, a \(5 \times 5\) matrix, and one scalar.

5.2 Server One-Shot Aggregation

The server aggregates client statistics in a single pass:

\[M_T^{-1} = M_0^{-1} + \sum_{t=1}^T \Delta M_t^{-1}, \quad m_T = m_0 + \sum_{t=1}^T \Delta m_t, \quad \nu_T = \nu_0 + \sum_{t=1}^T n_t\]

Summing across all \(T\) clients telescopes to yield the global scale matrix \(\Psi_T\):

\[\Psi_T = \Psi_0 + \sum_{t=1}^T \Delta Q_t + m_0^{\top} M_0 m_0 - m_T^{\top} M_T m_T\]

The central server draws global posterior samples directly from \(IW(\nu_T, \Psi_T)\) and \(MN(M_T m_T, M_T, \Sigma)\).

6 Empirical Analysis: Custom Federated Sampler (mniwSamplerFederated)

Loading data from ../data/X.txt and ../data/Y.txt, partitioning across \(T = 5\) federated clients, and comparing single-pass federated estimation against full single-server batch updates.

# Ingest dataset files
X_raw  <- as.matrix(read.table("../data/X.txt"))
Y_raw  <- as.matrix(read.table("../data/Y.txt"))
X_full <- cbind(1, X_raw)
Y_full <- Y_raw

p_dim <- ncol(X_full)
q_dim <- ncol(Y_full)

# Global prior parameters
m0     <- matrix(0, nrow = p_dim, ncol = q_dim)
M0_inv <- diag(1, p_dim)
nu0    <- q_dim + 2
Psi0   <- diag(1, q_dim)

# Partition data across T = 5 clients
T_clients   <- 5
client_idxs <- split(seq_len(nrow(X_full)), cut(seq_len(nrow(X_full)), T_clients, labels = FALSE))
client_data_list <- lapply(client_idxs, function(idx) {
  list(X = X_full[idx, ], Y = Y_full[idx, ])
})

# 1. Federated Learning Sampler (Custom R)
set.seed(42)
res_fed_custom <- mniwSamplerFederated(client_data_list, m0, M0_inv, nu0, Psi0, n_samples = 2000)

# 2. Single-Server Full Batch Sampler
full_server_data <- list(list(X = X_full, Y = Y_full))
set.seed(42)
res_batch_custom <- mniwSamplerFederated(full_server_data, m0, M0_inv, nu0, Psi0, n_samples = 2000)

6.1 Parameter Precision Comparison (Custom Sampler)

diff_m     <- max(abs(res_fed_custom$post_params$m - res_batch_custom$post_params$m))
diff_M_inv <- max(abs(res_fed_custom$post_params$M_inv - res_batch_custom$post_params$M_inv))
diff_Psi   <- max(abs(res_fed_custom$post_params$Psi - res_batch_custom$post_params$Psi))
diff_nu    <- abs(res_fed_custom$post_params$nu - res_batch_custom$post_params$nu)

param_comp <- data.frame(
  Parameter_Matrix = c("Location Vector (m)", "Precision Matrix (M^{-1})", "Scale Matrix (Psi)", "Degrees of Freedom (nu)"),
  Max_Absolute_Difference = c(diff_m, diff_M_inv, diff_Psi, diff_nu)
)

kable(param_comp, digits = 16, caption = "Numerical Equivalence: Federated vs. Single Server (Custom Sampler)")

7 Empirical Analysis: C++ Accelerated Federated Sampler (mniwSamplerFederated_rmniw)

Running federated estimation with mniwSamplerFederated_rmniw, passing precision \(\Omega = M_T^{-1}\) directly to C++ accelerated mniw::rmniw.

# 1. Federated Learning Sampler (rmniw)
set.seed(42)
res_fed_rmniw <- mniwSamplerFederated_rmniw(client_data_list, m0, M0_inv, nu0, Psi0, n_samples = 2000)

# 2. Single-Server Full Batch Sampler (rmniw)
set.seed(42)
res_batch_rmniw <- mniwSamplerFederated_rmniw(full_server_data, m0, M0_inv, nu0, Psi0, n_samples = 2000)

7.1 Parameter Precision Comparison (rmniw Sampler)

diff_m_rmniw     <- max(abs(res_fed_rmniw$post_params$m - res_batch_rmniw$post_params$m))
diff_M_inv_rmniw <- max(abs(res_fed_rmniw$post_params$M_inv - res_batch_rmniw$post_params$M_inv))
diff_Psi_rmniw   <- max(abs(res_fed_rmniw$post_params$Psi - res_batch_rmniw$post_params$Psi))
diff_nu_rmniw    <- abs(res_fed_rmniw$post_params$nu - res_batch_rmniw$post_params$nu)

param_comp_rmniw <- data.frame(
  Parameter_Matrix = c("Location Vector (m)", "Precision Matrix (M^{-1})", "Scale Matrix (Psi)", "Degrees of Freedom (nu)"),
  Max_Absolute_Difference = c(diff_m_rmniw, diff_M_inv_rmniw, diff_Psi_rmniw, diff_nu_rmniw)
)

kable(param_comp_rmniw, digits = 16, caption = "Numerical Equivalence: Federated vs. Single Server (rmniw Sampler)")

8 Execution Timing Benchmark

Comparing global sampling execution time across 10,000 posterior draws between custom R composition sampling and C++ accelerated sampling.

n_bench <- 10000

t_custom <- system.time({
  res_bench_custom <- mniwSamplerFederated(client_data_list, m0, M0_inv, nu0, Psi0, n_samples = n_bench)
})["elapsed"]

t_rmniw <- system.time({
  res_bench_rmniw <- mniwSamplerFederated_rmniw(client_data_list, m0, M0_inv, nu0, Psi0, n_samples = n_bench)
})["elapsed"]

timing_df <- data.frame(
  Sampler_Implementation = c("Custom R Sampler (mniwSamplerFederated)", 
                             "C++ Accelerated Sampler (mniwSamplerFederated_rmniw)"),
  Elapsed_Time_Sec = c(as.numeric(t_custom), as.numeric(t_rmniw)),
  Speedup_Factor   = c(1.0, as.numeric(t_custom / t_rmniw))
)

kable(timing_df, digits = 4, caption = paste0("Federated Sampling Execution Time Comparison (", n_bench, " Samples)"))
Federated Sampling Execution Time Comparison (10000 Samples)
Sampler_Implementation Elapsed_Time_Sec Speedup_Factor
Custom R Sampler (mniwSamplerFederated) 0.514 1.0000
C++ Accelerated Sampler (mniwSamplerFederated_rmniw) 0.022 23.3636

The C++ sampling implementation via mniw::rmniw achieves substantial performance speedup while preserving exact statistical equivalence with the full centralized model.
